title: a propagation in a repeated loop header compiles and is re-evaluated on every iteration
notes: Flipped from a VIBE1703 refusal certification on 2026-09-05 under the reference's delimiter lowering. The loop runs index 0,1,2 against a per-iteration limit(key)! of 3, so the printed 3 is the sum 0+1+2 — a value that is only correct if the propagation was NOT hoisted to a single pre-loop evaluation (a hoisted lowering computes the same bound but a re-evaluated one is what the authored program says; the failure direction — limit throwing on a later iteration — stays observable through the count function's own Result channel). The main was added with the flip; the authored lines above it are untouched so the fork's refusal position stays pinned in the marker.
